author: Seong Hyeon Choi
description:
Donald Trump’s demands that American allies in the Asia-Pacific region share more of the defensive burden have renewed questions about how far they can rely on the United States to help deter the likes of China and North Korea.
Such concerns have led to an increasing focus on developing their own defence industries – but analysts have said that may eventually weaken American dominance in the global arms trade.
Questions over Washington’s commitment
In the National Security Strategy released in...
title: How Trump’s call for Asia-Pacific allies to raise defence spending may backfire on US

author: Igor Patrick
description:
Brazil overtook Russia and Belgium in the first five months of this year to become the world’s largest importer of Chinese cars, buying US$5.2 billion worth of vehicles as brands raced to land shipments before a tariff increase took effect in July.
The figure, drawn from Chinese customs data, is up 146.9 per cent from the US$2.1 billion recorded a year earlier, when Brazil ranked sixth among buyers. Russia bought US$5 billion over the same months this year and Belgium purchased US$3.8...
title: Brazil becomes world’s top buyer of Chinese cars as imports jump 147%

author: Nayan Seth
description:
China may increasingly seek to use its dominance in the global electric vehicle industry as geopolitical leverage, giving Beijing greater influence over countries dependent on its technology and supply chains, according to analysts.
“With China, the strategy is different. It’s to overwhelm the industry, capture it, and use it ultimately as leverage,” said Michael Dunne, CEO of Dunne Insights, an auto advisory firm.
“When it comes to crunch time, they say, ‘Oh, by the way, we’re the source of all...
title: Can China’s EV boom give it decisive edge in geopolitical tech war?

author: Teresa Elena Frontado
description:
The United States on Wednesday sanctioned a group of mainland Chinese and Hong Kong shipping companies accused of operating vessels that transported Iranian oil to China, extending Washington’s economic campaign against Tehran alongside its naval blockade.
The US State Department said eight companies were designated for operating vessels that moved Iranian crude oil and petrochemical products to China and the United Arab Emirates as part of Iran’s sanctions-evading “shadow fleet”.
Six of the...
title: US sanctions Chinese, Hong Kong shipping firms over Iranian oil deliveries

author: Han Li
description:
Anthony Fauci repeatedly invoked his constitutional right against self-incrimination at a contentious US Senate hearing on Wednesday, refusing to answer questions about American funding for coronavirus research in China and allegations that he misled Congress about the origins of Covid-19.
The extraordinary appearance reopened one of Washington’s most politically divisive disputes: whether the pandemic began through natural transmission from animals or a laboratory-related incident in Wuhan, and...
title: Fauci refuses to answer questions at heated Senate hearing on Covid-19 origins

author: Dannie Peng
description:
The death of a six-year-old girl after receiving an experimental gene-editing therapy has been described by scientists as a tragedy that highlights the need to improve trial safeguards.
But some in the biotechnology industry fear Chinese policymakers may curtail the regulatory flexibility that scientists have long enjoyed in initiating clinical trials – a key mechanism behind China’s competitive edge in frontier treatments.


“I hope this tragedy does not have a lasting negative impact on...
title: Is China’s biotech boom at risk? Fear of policy backlash after death in gene-editing trial

author: Holly Chik
description:
Copies of the official paper of the Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region Committee of the Communist Party of China are not usually a hot commodity.
But the Saturday edition of Guangxi Daily became an overnight collector’s item after its front-page story on Wang Hong – who last week received the prestigious Fields Medal alongside her compatriot Deng Yu – went viral online.
Wang, who hails from the southern region, took home the highest honour for mathematicians under the age of 40 on July 23. Both...
title: Scalpers snap up local paper after profile on Fields winner Wang Hong goes viral

author: Gabriel Dominguez
description:
As the Chinese military expands its autonomous underwater capabilities, the US Coast Guard is seeking new ways to counter undersea drones, highlighting what analysts describe as a gap in America’s defence.
The law enforcement agency said it was requesting information on commercially available systems capable of detecting, tracking and disabling unmanned underwater vehicles (UUVs).
While the July 24 notice does not mention China, it comes less than a year after Beijing unveiled several uncrewed...
title: Can the US fend off China’s subsea drones? Its coastguard looks for answers

author: Alyssa Chen
description:
Philippine Defence Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jnr has urged greater vigilance over academic exchange programmes with China following reports that language teachers in Manila had been trained by a Chinese university at the centre of a recent controversy over the Batanes Islands.
Speaking in Manila on Wednesday, Teodoro cautioned that foreign-linked educational initiatives risked being exploited as conduits for grey-zone influence and state-sponsored disinformation.
His remarks followed a report...
title: Philippine defence chief warns Chinese teaching exchanges pose grey-zone threat

author: Victoria Bela
description:
Chinese scientists have used detailed satellite imagery analysis to examine damage to US military bases in the Middle East, uncovering discrepancies in both Washington and Tehran’s claims over the scale of the conflict.
Using advanced remote sensing and image-processing techniques, researchers from the Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS) also identified damage patterns that exposed vulnerabilities in fixed overseas military installations and highlighted operational shortcomings on either...
title: Chinese satellite imagery analysis challenges US-Iran war claims

author: Albee Zhang
description:
Chinese state media has shown the country’s first Type 076 amphibious assault ship, the Sichuan, computer-generated footage of how it launches GJ-21 stealth fighter drones and quotes from a military commentator who said the vessel was in the final stages of commissioning.
The 40,000-tonne ship, featuring a 250-metre-long and 62-metre-wide (820 feet by 203 feet) flight deck, recently completed deck line markings, meaning it entered the final testing phase, military expert Wei Dongxu told state...
title: China’s Type 076 amphibious assault ship Sichuan in final tests with drone catapult

author: Dulue Mbachu
description:
China has overtaken the United States in terms of positive perceptions among young Africans, though Washington is still seen as more influential than Beijing, according to a survey published on Wednesday.
The African Youth Survey polled 4,901 respondents aged 18 to 24 and split equally between males and females, in 16 of Africa’s 54 countries, asking them which foreign powers had influence on their country.
The report said 81 per cent agreed that the US was influential, while 79 per cent...
title: ‘Practical’ young Africans leaning towards China over US and away from ideology

author: Shaoshan Liu
description:
China’s emerging advantage in artificial intelligence (AI) is not that it already has the world’s best chips or strongest frontier models. It is that Chinese companies are increasingly providing capable intelligence at a price the global market can afford.
AI is fast becoming everyday infrastructure. It is metered by usage and embedded in businesses, public services and devices, much like electricity or cloud computing. In an infrastructure market, leadership depends on affordability,...
title: China should lean into its defining AI advantage – accessibility

author: Caroline Lin
description:
Beijing has launched a drone research hub in Tibet near Mount Everest in an effort to exploit its high-altitude advantage in the ongoing competition for technological dominance between the US and China.
The Plateau Drone R&D Application Centre was recently unveiled by Xizang University, state news agency Xinhua reported earlier this month. Xizang is the official Chinese pinyin name for the Tibet autonomous region in western China.
Situated on the Chinese side of the world’s highest peak, the...
title: A new peak in US-China tech rivalry? Tibet drone hub launches on Mount Everest

author: SCMP
description:
We have put together stories from our coverage on science from the past two weeks to help you stay informed. If you would like to see more of our reporting, please consider subscribing.
1. Chinese scientists have bad news on having babies in space
If the future of humanity lies in the vast expanse of space, could humans actually perpetuate the species beyond Earth? As a team of Chinese scientists has discovered – the outlook is not very positive.
2. China plans to strengthen Great Green Wall...
title: Having babies in space; China’s first Fields Medal winners: 7 science highlights

author: Dulue Mbachu
description:
International students once saw US colleges as a gateway to a world-class education and career head start but shifting United States immigration policies, tightening visa conditions and high-profile ICE raids are causing them to reconsider. Dulue Mbachu looks at how African students are altering their education plans during the second Trump administration. The first instalment in our series is here.
For 23-year-old Kunle Adeyemi, it took some time to overcome the disappointment of being denied a...
title: Spurned by the US, African students turn to China for a university degree

author: Nayan Seth,Han Li
description:
A senior Pentagon official on Tuesday said US-China military communication was “stronger than it has been in years”, marking a rare bright spot in the broader strategic rivalry between the world’s two most powerful countries.
“Under the leadership of Secretary [Pete] Hegseth, we are actively repairing a once broken military-to-military channel and making clear, steady progress,” said Alvaro Smith, deputy assistant defence secretary for China, Taiwan and Mongolia.
He made the remarks during a...
title: Pentagon official hails ‘stronger’ military ties with PLA at anniversary event

author: Lawrence Chung
description:
The United States has released a rare photo of the American and Taiwanese coastguards operating together at sea, as Beijing expands maritime law enforcement in waters east of the island.
The American Institute in Taiwan (AIT) – the de facto US embassy in Taipei – posted the undated image on social media on Tuesday, saying the two sides were coordinating on search, rescue, disaster relief and maritime law enforcement.
“The United States appreciates Taiwan’s partnership in maritime security and...
title: US posts photo of coastguard working with Taiwan after Beijing starts patrols

author: Orange Wang
description:
Beijing should step in to fill the global “vacuum” in rules on artificial intelligence as a Chinese AI model opens up a policy divide in the United States, according to various institutions within China.
The calls came after Beijing-based start-up Moonshot AI launched its Kimi K3 model earlier this month, sending shock waves through Silicon Valley and the White House.
The model is reportedly almost as powerful as top US rivals and much cheaper.
Moonshot, which was founded just three years ago,...
title: Should China aim for the lead in making AI rules for the world?
